kind_of_no: owner-lot condo with no booking site (owner rentals / phone only)
why: Read 2026-10-30: the association's own site calusacampground.com (a Conduu condo-owner portal: About Us, Map, Amenities, Contact, owner login) calls Calusa Campground Condominium Association, Inc. 'a residential community comprised of 367 units' ('some units are land only others house recreational vehicles and residential homes') and has no rates, reservations page or booking engine, only an office phone (305-451-0232 ext. 101) and a contact form; RV Life lists no booking link (book_now_active false) and Good Sam gives no website; the RoverPass listing is unclaimed (isBookable false, API read 2026-10-30); no Campspot/Firefly/Newbook/Staylist listing found; the nights on sale online are individual owners' units and lots (Booking.com/Expedia/VRBO/Airbnb park models and RVs, and an owner's Hipcamp lot 'The Little Mermaid', not accepting bookings). Under AWH's owner-lot rule (2026-10-30) nights sold only by owners or by phone/email inquiry are a skip.
name: Calusa Campground Resort & Marina
flags: Owner-lot condo resort: 367 deeded units (20 bayfront, 104 on two canals, 243 inland per the association's About Us; the 2022 association map says 'This Map is for Rental Purposes Only'). The association publishes no rental-program lot count and no rental rates; Good Sam types it 'Condo park' with 'from $115/night' (undated), and Google lists it as a campground but its Prices tab shows only Booking.com/Travelmyth/Bluepillow owner-unit listings ($266 for 2 nights Oct 31-Nov 2, 6 guests).

Transient RV stays do happen, apparently through the office or owners by phone: RV Life reviews report motorhome stays on sites 446 (3/2025, $85), 518 (3/2024, $69 with Good Sam discount), 65 (3/2021, $95) and 447 (1/2019, $60), and Campendium reviewers 'reserved' canal sites (2019-2021). None names an online booking channel. If AWH counts an office phone reservation desk as enough, this would need a rate read by phone, which I can't do.

Quality signals if it is ever reconsidered: Google 4.1/492; RV Life reviewers call it 'mostly full-time residents/owners' (1/2019), 'a weird combination of $800,000-$1 million houses and crappy old trailers ... very tight' (3/2024), and complain of barking dogs and loud music (3/2025); Campendium 2020-2021 reviewers report reserved sites being switched at check-in. Several owner listings mention a three-day minimum rental policy (unverified).

Long-stay test 5 is also doubtful: the association calls itself a residential community and lots carry residential homes and mobile homes sold through realtors (MLS listings at 325 Calusa St), though no count of homes vs RV lots is published.
